name: eranos
summary: Eranos lets people donate unused AI tokens to build, test, and independently review off-the-shelf agent skills, read-only MCP tools, operational files (SOPs, checklists, CSV templates, Open Referral directories), and multi-step agentic processes for NGOs, nonprofits, and public-good teams. Contributors connect agents to scoped queues on Tessera (eq01 spec, eq02 build & test, eq03 independent review); deterministic checks verify SYNTHETIC test fixtures and step autonomy boundaries so interviews, crisis safety planning, individual decisions, and external sends stay strictly human-only; and a second contributor's agent or human steward (drafter != reviewer across both worker ID and Tessera key ID) approves each package before atomic compare-and-set publication into eranos.catalog. Alongside Shamash (shamash.<domain>), Eranos (eranos.<domain>) runs on Tessera (tessera.<domain>) under a single shared domain.

status.notes: Schemas, copy and topic guards, strict JSON loader, six NGO and nonprofit tracks, deterministic verifier, two-step Tessera pipeline (eq01 -> eq02 -> eq03) with steward park/resume and CAS catalog publication, traced local/HTTP adapter, FastAPI service with edge lockdown, React 19 + Astryx web app with offline snapshot mode, and task briefs E1-E4 built and tested (56 pytest tests, one of which needs a ta-amps-hackathon checkout alongside, plus Tessera's conformance suite through the adapter: 30 passed, 6 skipped).

components.title: Personal-data screen

components.title: Schemas and records
components.role: Strict Pydantic models for tracks, kit requests, agent skills, read-only MCP tools, autonomy boundaries, published kits, and briefs

components.title: Strict JSON loader
components.role: Loads track packs, kit bundles, and briefs while rejecting duplicate keys and NaN/Infinity

components.title: Track registry and packs

components.title: Deterministic kit verifier
components.role: Checks workflow autonomy boundaries, open SPDX allowlist, required human_only step kinds, MCP JSON Schema structure, HTTPS source citations, SYNTHETIC fixtures, and zero-storage practice verification

components.title: Queue stage contracts
components.role: Defines eq01 (spec), eq02 (draft), and eq03 (review) leased queue configurations on Tessera

components.title: Two-step volunteer pipeline

boundaries.rule: Static app and /api/* only; strict CSP, HSTS, nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on every response
When ERANOS_EDGE_SECRET is set, x-edge-auth must match in constant time except GET /api/health and public health/agent-discovery routes
No kit enters eranos.catalog unless deterministic verification passes and an independent reviewer (worker != drafter and key != drafter_key) approves it
Interviews, crisis safety planning, legal judgments, individual decisions, and external sends are refused unless marked human_only; MCP tools are read-only

invariants.statement: No kit, track, or fixture accuses a party or requests surveillance, scraping, or personal-data harvesting
Interviews, crisis safety plans, legal judgments, individual decisions, and external transmissions stay human_only
Every fixture carries the SYNTHETIC mark and strict JSON files refuse duplicate keys and NaN
Engine code is domain-neutral and names zero track IDs or kit IDs; tracks, custom domains, step kinds, and deliverable packs load as pure data
Single-agent publication is refused: drafter and reviewer must differ across both worker ID and Tessera key ID
Unverified drafts cannot be published even if an upstream worker forges a verification report
Sensitive kits park on Tessera for human nonprofit steward sign-off and publish atomically via CAS upon resume
Agent briefs never carry public effect, API routes reject invalid kit IDs and unauthenticated origin traffic, and private names never leak
A referenced example kit takes its content only from its seed pack: every pin matches the noun's digest, and every step matches its verb template's title and claimant

The site's example needs and example-run count come from nouns: each kit's need from its seed pack, and the count from one recorded run per example kit whose example and inputs still match their digests
Work by a tracked anonymous session is published or delivered only after review by a different keyed worker or a person; anonymous sessions never claim review verbs or write the catalog
A nonprofit's request becomes exactly one eq01 verb, which an authorized worker classifies and splits into public research and kit parts, recorded as a plan noun
Personal data is refused before a request is stored, and public reports cite a public source for every claim, say they are not legal advice when legal, and leave the decision to a person

No request is answered from the library without a reuse check that a key other than the planner's approves with a recorded model verdict; a check that says no or is unsure, or never finishes, has new work planned, and a wrongly reused request is opened again only by a reopen its own record names

import_rules.why: Ring 0 holds pure records, autonomy boundaries, and text safety rules with zero I/O or fabric dependencies
Ring 1 runs deterministic verification and strict JSON loading without touching Tessera, adapters, or network
Ring 2 orchestrates eq01 -> eq02 -> eq03 against an injected Tessera Backend port without knowing local SQLite vs HTTP
Ring 3 constructs backends and trace logs; it never calls the pipeline or HTTP/CLI doors
Ring 4 (API and CLI) are leaf entry points; nothing inward depends on them
Runtime package code never imports test, build, or deployment folders

claims.claim: Volunteer agents build across both anti-exploitation NGO tracks and everyday nonprofit operations tracks using one domain-neutral engine
Two-step Tessera verification guarantees drafter != reviewer across worker ID and key ID, with steward park/resume and atomic CAS publication
Interviews, crisis safety planning, legal judgments, individual decisions, and external sends are deterministically restricted to human_only
Hosted on Fly.io behind a Cloudflare Worker on eranos.<domain> alongside shamash.<domain> and tessera.<domain> under one shared domain

deployment.how: deploy/bootstrap-hosting.sh, then GitHub deploy workflow with approval
parts: Cloudflare Worker eranos (eranos.<domain>, static app and /api proxy)
Fly.io app eranos-api with a 1 GB volume

neutral: two-step eq01 -> eq02 -> eq03 pipeline and CAS publisher

extension_points.what: A new NGO or nonprofit track
extension_points.how: Add tracks/<id>/track.json specifying domain, organizations, agent_helps_with, human_must_do, required_human_only_kinds, and dated HTTPS sources
Submit a KitRequest to eq01, draft on eq02 with one volunteer agent, and approve on eq03 with an independent reviewer

limitations: Every example fixture is synthetic; real NGO deployments require local partner review of directory contacts and jurisdictional rules
MCP tool contracts in the catalog are specifications and schemas (read_only: true); organizations wire them to their own local spreadsheets or directories
Live custom-domain cutover awaits binding the shared root domain on the ta-amps Cloudflare zone
open_questions: Should tracks specify per-country helpline re-verification intervals shorter than 90 days?
Should high-impact kits require two independent volunteer reviewers in addition to a human nonprofit steward?

feedback.how: Open an issue on GitHub; docs/review.md lists the sharpest review questions
